title: Random Access Codes: Explicit Constructions, Optimality, and Classical-Quantum Gaps
summary: A random access code (RAC) encodes an $L$-bit string into a $k$-bit message, $L>k$, so that any requested bit can be recovered with high probability; a quantum RAC (QRAC) uses $k$ qubits instead. We give a geometric characterization of optimal classical $(L,k)$-RACs under average and worst-case decoding criteria. The average criterion is reduced to choosing $2^k$ representatives in $\{0,1\}^L$, while the worst-case criterion is reduced to a minimax problem over $2^k$ points in $[0,1]^L$ with a distance-like objective.
